response: Innate immunity is the first line of defense and includes components like the inflammatory response, phagocytes, complement, cytokines, and natural killer cells. It provides a rapid, non-specific defense against pathogens. Inherited defects in innate immunity, such as complement deficiencies, can lead to autoimmune diseases like lupus. Macrophage deficiencies, like in chronic granulomatous disease, result in susceptibility to specific pathogens. Aicardi-Goutières syndrome involves constitutive production of inflammatory cytokines, and lack of interferon responsiveness makes individuals more susceptible to viral infections. In contrast, adaptive immunity is specific and involves lymphocytes, with memory and antigen recognition capabilities. It provides a slower but more specific defense against pathogens. Mice lacking B and T cells exhibit symptoms of adaptive immunity deficiency, while those lacking innate responses show signs of both innate and adaptive deficiencies.
